name: Rune
description: Single source of truth for the Rune language. Derived from this file: the tree-sitter grammar, highlight query and scanner config (scripts/generate.mjs), the doc tables and the LLM language card (scripts/gen-lang-docs.ts), the engine's modifier/transport/fault/indent tables and its rule catalogue (loaded at runtime), and the codegen templates. Hand-edit here and regenerate.

tags.label: Requirement
tags.description: Feature entry point / happy path. Format: noun.verb(InputDto): OutputDto
tags.summary: A requirement — one feature entry point, the happy-path end-to-end. Input is a DTO (or inline {}), output is a DTO; the last step (or a [RET]) yields the output; faults live on its steps, not here; scope resets at each [REQ]. `[REQ:open]` is the openness marker — the endpoint is reachable without a credential (the only modifier [REQ] takes).

tags.label: Module
tags.summary: Names the module this file describes; fills the <module>/ path slot. The first non-comment line; kebab-case on disk. Optional (defaults to the filename). `[MOD] name: prose` plus indented continuation lines is the module's front-door description.

tags.label: Entrypoint
tags.summary: An inbound entrypoint (HTTP route) — the inverse of a boundary. Its body is ONE indented `[REQ] noun.verb(In): Out` line naming the coordinator it dispatches to (required — there is no signature matching). An optional `@ METHOD /template` clause between the name and the parens sets the verb and the route; `{field}` segments (and one trailing `{field*}` catch-all) bind URL parts to same-named input fields.

tags.label: Polymorphic step
tags.description: Opens a polymorphic block. The noun names an interface; each [CSE] is a concrete case.
tags.summary: Opens a polymorphic block where the noun names an interface. Each [CSE] is a concrete implementation; they all share the interface's return type, and each case's last step yields it. The block ends at the first line indented no deeper than the [PLY] (the one place relative indentation carries meaning).

tags.label: Case
tags.description: A concrete case inside a [PLY] block. Followed by a camelCase case name.
tags.summary: A concrete case inside a [PLY] block (camelCase name), with its own sub-steps and faults, indented deeper than the [PLY].

tags.label: Constructor
tags.description: Constructor shorthand. Instantiates a [NON] and adds it to scope. No parens, no return type.
tags.summary: Constructor shorthand — instantiates a declared [NON] and adds it to scope under its own name. No parentheses, no return type; construction details are an implementation concern.

tags.label: Return
tags.description: Return a value already created earlier in the flow. The value must be in scope.
tags.summary: Returns a value already in scope — by its name (`[RET] loaded`) or, for an unnamed value, by its type (`[RET] TaskDto`). Use it when the last step is a side effect. Redundant right after a step that already returns the output.

tags.label: Type definition
tags.description: Defines a named semantic type that resolves to a primitive. Format: name: primitive
tags.summary: A named semantic type built on a primitive (string, number, boolean, void, Uint8Array). Gives meaning to a raw primitive — `id` vs `string`. Generics (Array<url>), tuples ([x, y]) and string enums ("a" | "b" — generated as a quoted union validated with @IsIn) are allowed. A [TYP] never resolves to a DTO; a noun is a [NON], never `[TYP] x: Class`. The bracket slot is a comma-separated modifier list: [TYP:ext,uuid], [TYP:min=0,max=100].

tags.label: DTO definition
tags.description: Defines a reusable data contract. Name must end in Dto. Format: NameDto: prop1, prop2
tags.summary: A reusable data contract; the name must end in Dto. Properties reference types or other DTOs by name; `url(s)` is `urls: Array<url>`, `tag(s?)` an array whose elements are not validated (dirty inbound data), `name?` an optional property. A description is required on the next line. `[DTO:core]` routes it to src/core; `[DTO:open]` is an opaque inbound payload — declared fields are validated, undeclared fields ride through. Every DTO must be used.

tags.label: Noun declaration
tags.description: Declares a noun (subject) with a prose description on the following lines.
tags.summary: Declares a noun (a subject / class) with a prose description on the following lines. [NEW] instantiates it; instance steps `noun.verb()` need it in scope; static steps `Noun::verb()` do not. Every [NON] must be used.

tags.label: Service declaration
tags.description: Declares a backing service: a transport (SDK/HTTP/WEBSOCKET/SIDECAR/NATIVE), a name referenced by service: boundary prefixes, its required env vars, and a required @docs link.
tags.summary: Declares a backing service — transport (one of the registry's transports, in parens), a name referenced by `service:` boundary prefixes, its env vars, a one-line prose description and a required `@docs <url>` line. Declared once, in src/core/core.rune; boundary calls reference it as service:noun.verb(...).

dtoSuffix.description: An identifier ending in Dto is a DTO reference.

fault.description: Fault lines: lowercase, hyphen-separated, indented under a step.

lint.message: line exceeds {max} characters ({found})
lint.fix: wrap the line; a fault line may continue on the next `! ` line, prose on the next indented line
lint.doc: Every line is at most the registry's column limit so a spec reads in any editor and diffs line by line.

lint.message: {tag} should be indented {expected} spaces (found {found})
lint.doc: Indentation is presentation, owned by `rune fmt`: the registry's indent table says where each tag sits. The checker warns; it never changes meaning.

lint.message: [MOD] needs a name — {syntax}
lint.doc: The module directive names the module; an empty name cannot fill the src/<module>/ slot.

lint.message: [MOD] invalid name "{name}" — must start with a letter or "_" and use only letters, digits, "-", "_"
lint.doc: A [MOD] name becomes a directory AND a JS identifier alias in the generated bootstrap registry, so it must be an identifier shape.

lint.message: duplicate [MOD]: already set to "{module}"
lint.doc: A .rune file describes exactly one module.

lint.message: no [MOD] directive and could not derive module name
lint.doc: Without a [MOD] the module name comes from the spec's filename; a path the engine cannot map to a module needs the directive.

lint.message: [REQ] missing or malformed signature — {syntax}
lint.doc: A requirement is noun.verb(InputDto): OutputDto.

lint.message: [REQ] unknown modifier "{modifier}" — the only one is :open
lint.doc: [REQ] takes exactly one modifier, the openness marker.

lint.message: [REQ:core] is invalid — coordinators are module-level
lint.doc: core/ has no coordinators/ slot; a requirement always belongs to its module.

lint.message: [ENT] missing or malformed signature — {syntax}
lint.doc: An entrypoint is surface.action(InputDto): OutputDto, optionally with `@ METHOD /template` between the name and the parens.

lint.message: [ENT] HTTP method must be one of GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE (got "{method}")
lint.doc: The route clause's verb is an HTTP method.

lint.message: [ENT] body [REQ] has a malformed signature
lint.doc: The body line names the coordinator with its full signature.

lint.message: [ENT] body [REQ] does not take a modifier
lint.doc: Openness is declared on the top-level [REQ], not repeated in the body reference.

lint.message: [ENT] {surface}.{action} names no [REQ] — add an indented `[REQ] noun.verb({input}): {output}` line under it{candidates}
lint.doc: An entrypoint dispatches to exactly the [REQ] its body names. There is no matching by signature: two [REQ]s with the same (input, output) would make the pick silent and wrong.

lint.message: [ENT] {surface}.{action} delegates to [REQ] {noun}.{verb}, which is not defined
lint.doc: The body [REQ] must exist in the same spec.

lint.message: [SRV] malformed — expected [SRV] (TRANSPORT)<name>: <ENV,…>
lint.doc: A service declaration is a parenthesized transport, a name, and its env vars.

lint.message: [SRV] unknown transport "{transport}" — expected {transports}
lint.doc: Transports are the registry's closed set.

lint.message: [SRV] {service}: @docs needs a URL
lint.doc: The documentation link is the one piece of provenance a dev needs to wire the service.

lint.message: [SRV] {service}: duplicate @docs link
lint.doc: One documentation link per service.

lint.message: [SRV] {service} requires an @docs <url> line
lint.doc: Every service declares where its documentation lives.

lint.message: [SRV] ({transport}){service} declared in a module spec — shared services must be declared once in {core}
lint.fix: move the [SRV] to {core} and delete it here
lint.doc: Services are shared infrastructure, declared exactly once in src/core/core.rune and resolved from there by every module.

lint.message: no core.rune found under the resolved project root "{root}" — shared services live in its src/core/core.rune and none was found there, so the boundary service{plural} {services} cannot be resolved. Pass `--root <project-dir>` or move the spec into that project.
lint.doc: Boundary services resolve against the project's core spec; a root with no core.rune is almost always a mis-resolved root.

lint.message: undeclared service "{service}"
lint.doc: A boundary prefix names a declared service; there are no built-in boundary kinds.

lint.message: [DTO] missing properties — {syntax}
lint.doc: A DTO lists its properties after the colon.

lint.message: [DTO] unknown modifier "{modifier}" — expected :core or :open
lint.doc: A typo here would silently degrade to a strict DTO that strips an inbound payload's fields at runtime.

lint.message: [DTO] {dto}: property "{prop}" has no [TYP] or [DTO]
lint.doc: Every property resolves to a declared type — a [TYP], a nested [DTO] (named directly or via the <Name>Dto convention) — so no generated field is `unknown`.

lint.message: [TYP] missing type — {syntax}
lint.doc: A type declaration names its primitive after the colon.

lint.message: [TYP] unknown modifier "{modifier}" (allowed: {allowed})
lint.doc: The bracket slot takes only the registry's modifiers.

lint.message: [TYP] modifier "{modifier}" requires a {base} type, but "{name}" is {type}
lint.doc: A constraint fits only its base primitive: string constraints on string types, number constraints on number types.

lint.message: [TYP] modifier "{modifier}" requires a {kind} value (e.g. {example})
lint.doc: min/max take a numeric value; example/from take text.

lint.message: [TYP] modifier "{modifier}" does not take a value
lint.doc: Only valued modifiers are written with `=`.

lint.message: [TYP] modifier "{modifier}" must be one of {values} (got "{value}")
lint.doc: A closed-set modifier rejects anything outside its set.

lint.message: [TYP:from={value}] is retired — path segments are bound by the [ENT]'s route template
lint.fix: write the route as `[ENT] surface.action @ METHOD /…/{{{name}}}(In): Out` (`{{{name}*}}` for a catch-all) and drop from={value}
lint.doc: One form per concept: the route template on the [ENT] is the only path binding.

lint.message: [TYP] {name}: Class is retired — a noun is a [NON]
lint.fix: replace it with `[NON] {name}` and a description
lint.doc: [NON] declares a noun; [TYP] declares a primitive-backed type. Class was the second spelling of the first.

lint.message: [NON] missing name — {syntax}
lint.doc: A noun declaration names its subject.

lint.message: [PLY] missing or malformed signature — {syntax}
lint.doc: A polymorphic step has the shape of a step.

lint.message: [PLY] outside [REQ]
lint.doc: Steps, including polymorphic ones, live under a requirement.

lint.message: nested [PLY] inside [CSE] not supported
lint.doc: One level of polymorphism per step.

lint.message: [PLY] {noun}.{verb} requires at least one [CSE] (a polymorphic step needs ≥1 variant case)
lint.doc: A [PLY] with no case generates a barrel pointing at nothing.

lint.message: [CSE] missing case name — {syntax}
lint.doc: A case names its variant.

lint.message: [CSE] outside [PLY] block
lint.doc: A case belongs to the polymorphic block above it.

lint.message: [NEW] missing noun — {syntax}
lint.doc: [NEW] names the [NON] it instantiates.

lint.message: [CTR] is retired — write `[NEW] {noun}`
lint.doc: One spelling per concept.

lint.message: [RET] missing value — {syntax}
lint.doc: [RET] names the value it returns.

lint.message: {service}: malformed signature — service:noun.verb(args): type
lint.doc: A boundary step is the service prefix followed by a step signature.

lint.message: step outside [REQ]: {kind}
lint.doc: Every step belongs to the [REQ] above it.

lint.message: ! fault line must follow a step
lint.doc: A fault belongs to the step that raises it.

lint.message: fault name "{name}" must be lowercase, hyphen-separated (optionally =STATUS)
lint.doc: Fault names are slugs: they become test names and class names.

lint.message: bare fault line — faults are written `! {names}`
lint.fix: prefix the line with `! ` (`rune fmt` does this)
lint.doc: The `!` marker declares the line's kind, so indentation never has to.

lint.message: fault "{name}" is not well-known and carries no status
lint.fix: write `! {name}=<HTTP status>` or use a well-known fault ({wellKnown})
lint.doc: The runtime maps every fault to an HTTP status: well-known names from the registry, custom names from their declared status.

lint.message: unrecognized line: "{text}"
lint.doc: Every line is a tag, a step, a fault, a service doc link, or prose under a declaration.

lint.message: DTO name "{name}" must end in {suffix}
lint.doc: The suffix marks a validated contract everywhere it is referenced.

lint.message: [DTO] {name} needs a description on the next line
lint.doc: The description is the contract's meaning; codegen puts it on the class.

lint.message: requirement input "{input}" must be a DTO or inline {}
lint.doc: Inputs are validated at the seam; only a DTO carries a contract.

lint.message: requirement output "{output}" must be a DTO
lint.doc: Outputs are validated at the seam; only a DTO carries a contract.

lint.message: {service}: boundary params/return must be DTO or primitive — got {bad}
lint.doc: Only DTOs and primitives cross a system boundary.

lint.message: {key} has an inconsistent signature ({got} vs {first})
lint.doc: The same noun.verb has one signature throughout the document; the first occurrence defines it.

lint.message: [REQ] {key} is declared twice
lint.doc: One requirement per noun.verb — a second declaration would overwrite the first coordinator.

lint.message: [TYP] {name} is defined more than once
lint.doc: Names are unique per kind.

lint.message: [DTO] {name} is defined more than once
lint.doc: Names are unique per kind.

lint.message: [NON] {name} is defined more than once
lint.doc: Names are unique per kind.

lint.message: [TYP] {name} is never used
lint.doc: A declared type no DTO or step references is dead vocabulary.

lint.message: [DTO] {name} is never used
lint.doc: A declared contract nothing references is dead vocabulary.

lint.message: [NON] {name} is never used
lint.doc: A declared noun no step instantiates or calls is dead vocabulary.

lint.message: step "{step}" is missing a return type
lint.fix: write `: void` for a side effect
lint.doc: Every step declares what it yields; a side effect yields void.

lint.message: last step must return {output} (the REQ output), got {got}
lint.doc: A requirement ends by yielding its output: its last step returns it, or a [RET] names it.

lint.message: [TYP] {name} must be a primitive — it can't reference DTO {ref}
lint.doc: A [TYP] aliases a primitive; a DTO is referenced by name.

lint.message: instance noun "{noun}" isn't in scope (use :: for static, or [NEW] it, or return it from an earlier step)
lint.doc: An instance step operates on a value; the noun must be live in the requirement's scope.

lint.message: parameter "{param}" isn't in scope (return it from a prior step or take it from the input DTO)
lint.doc: A step consumes only values in scope: the input DTO, its fields, and earlier results.

lint.message: "{ref}" is not a defined [TYP], [DTO], [NON], or primitive
lint.doc: Every type a step or DTO names is declared.

lint.message: a value named "{name}" is already in scope (from {from})
lint.doc: One live value per name; a value's default name is its type, so a second value of the same type must be named with `as`.

lint.message: [RET] {value} is redundant — the step above already returns it
lint.doc: A [RET] exists for a flow whose last step is a side effect.

lint.message: input field "{field}" of {ent} has no producer and no example
lint.doc: A required input field nothing produces is a guaranteed 422 in the cake/headless walk unless its [TYP] carries an example.

lint.message: [ENT] {surface}.{action} is a {method} — model a command verb instead of editing a record
lint.doc: The waist rule: reads are GET queries returning current-state DTOs; writes are POST command verbs. PUT/PATCH exist only for an upstream contract you don't control.

lint.message: verb "{verb}" is a JavaScript reserved word and cannot name a generated function
lint.doc: Verbs become exported function and method names in the generated code.

lint.message: generated DTO is missing runtime validation (class-validator / zod)
lint.doc: generated DTO is missing runtime validation (class-validator / zod)

lint.message: fault "{fault}" from {req} has no Deno.test in the generated tests
lint.doc: fault "{fault}" from {req} has no Deno.test in the generated tests

lint.message: generated file uses a "../" relative import — use an @ alias
lint.doc: generated file uses a "../" relative import — use an @ alias

lint.message: generated file imports npm:/jsr: directly — use a # alias
lint.doc: generated file imports npm:/jsr: directly — use a # alias

lint.message: integration file doesn't reference its DTO {dto}
lint.doc: integration file doesn't reference its DTO {dto}

lint.message: {from} layer may not import {to} layer ({spec})
lint.doc: {from} layer may not import {to} layer ({spec})

lint.message: re-exports are only allowed in mod-root / poly-mod / bootstrap files
lint.doc: re-exports are only allowed in mod-root / poly-mod / bootstrap files

lint.message: import into a poly structure must go through poly-mod ({spec})
lint.doc: import into a poly structure must go through poly-mod ({spec})

lint.message: module {from} may not import module {to}'s internals ({spec}) — use core/ or its mod-root
lint.doc: module {from} may not import module {to}'s internals ({spec}) — use core/ or its mod-root

lint.message: data-layer method returns a raw object — return a validated instance (assert/plainToInstance)
lint.doc: data-layer method returns a raw object — return a validated instance (assert/plainToInstance)

lint.message: coordinator casts to "{dto}" — validate the seam with assert({dto}, ...) instead of a blind cast
lint.doc: coordinator casts to "{dto}" — validate the seam with assert({dto}, ...) instead of a blind cast

lint.message: {count} sibling features export {name} with compatible signatures — extract a poly structure
lint.doc: {count} sibling features export {name} with compatible signatures — extract a poly structure

lint.message: feature extends poly base {base} — it likely belongs inside that poly structure
lint.doc: feature extends poly base {base} — it likely belongs inside that poly structure

lint.message: directory "{name}" is not allowed — name folders by role, not as generic buckets
lint.doc: directory "{name}" is not allowed — name folders by role, not as generic buckets

lint.message: loose grab-bag file "{name}" — put code in a named feature/role folder
lint.doc: loose grab-bag file "{name}" — put code in a named feature/role folder

lint.message: module {module} has only {count} source files (< {min}) — consider consolidating
lint.doc: module {module} has only {count} source files (< {min}) — consider consolidating

lint.message: file sits in a rune-managed slot but no rune element declares it (orphan)
lint.doc: file sits in a rune-managed slot but no rune element declares it (orphan)

lint.message: heal-rules entry still carries todo: true — enrich it (strict-gated: errors under rune lint --strict)
lint.doc: heal-rules entry still carries todo: true — enrich it (strict-gated: errors under rune lint --strict)

modifiers.label: Core
modifiers.description: Routes an element to the shared kernel (src/core/…) instead of the current module. Core elements are importable from any module; module elements are not. Allowed on [DTO] and [TYP]; not on [REQ].

modifiers.label: Open
modifiers.description: The OPENNESS MARKER: this endpoint is reachable WITHOUT a credential. Codegen emits it as `access: "open"` on the generated @Endpoint, which surfaces as `x-bedrock-auth` on the operation's OpenAPI — where the backend's policy table comes from. An unmarked [REQ] is authenticated (the backend slot's default). The only modifier [REQ] takes.

modifiers.label: External
modifiers.description: Marks a type whose value is produced OUTSIDE this module (another module's endpoint, a human). Entrypoint codegen turns unproduced input fields of this type into $name external-input binds (ghost stubs mint them in dev). Composes with constraint modifiers: [TYP:ext,uuid].

modifiers.label: UUID
modifiers.description: Constrains a string [TYP] to UUID format (class-validator @IsUUID).

modifiers.label: Email
modifiers.description: Constrains a string [TYP] to email format (class-validator @IsEmail).

modifiers.label: URL
modifiers.description: Constrains a string [TYP] to URL format (class-validator @IsUrl).

modifiers.label: Non-empty
modifiers.description: Constrains a string [TYP] to be non-empty (class-validator @IsNotEmpty).

modifiers.label: JSON
modifiers.description: Marks a string [TYP] that carries a JSON-encoded object/array over the wire (no typed [DTO]); validates it PARSES at the boundary (class-validator @IsJSON) so invalid JSON 422s at the seam instead of degrading silently downstream.

modifiers.label: Integer
modifiers.description: Constrains a number [TYP] to integers (class-validator @IsInt, replacing @IsNumber).

modifiers.label: Minimum
modifiers.description: Constrains a number [TYP] to a minimum value (class-validator @Min(N)).

modifiers.label: Maximum
modifiers.description: Constrains a number [TYP] to a maximum value (class-validator @Max(N)).

modifiers.label: Positive
modifiers.description: Constrains a number [TYP] to be positive (class-validator @IsPositive).

modifiers.label: Example
modifiers.description: A real sample value for the field, emitted as @ApiProperty({ example }) — keep's runner and cake fill required, unbound input fields from it so headless walks don't 422. The value runs to the next comma/], so it cannot contain a comma. Composes: [TYP:ext,example=orders].

modifiers.label: From
modifiers.description: Field-source binding (OpenAPI's parameter model): where this field is populated from at the HTTP boundary — query | header. Body is the default, so a field with no from= routes exactly as before. Path segments are bound by the [ENT]'s `@ METHOD /path/{field}` route template, never by a modifier. Composes: [TYP:from=query,example=widgets].

bootstrap/.$desc: Composition root — wires modules, starts the app

mod.desc: app entry point and module wiring

modules.desc: module registry — generated by rune sync as runes are added/removed

stubs.desc: ghost-stub registry — generated by rune sync to mint placeholders for unfulfilled [TYP:ext] inputs; evaporates once every external input has a real producer

core/.$desc: Shared kernel — importable from any module

core.desc: shared-service rune spec — the single [SRV] declaration site for the whole project

mod.desc: pure logic, no I/O or side effects

test.desc: unit tests for the sibling mod

poly-mod.desc: barrel re-export for the active variant

mod.desc: optional dispatcher: selects + delegates to a variant for non-trivial dispatch (co-located _-prefixed helpers also allowed)
cross-cutting orchestration importable from any module (e.g. an auth guard) — may use core business + data

int.test.desc: integration test for the shared workflow

<module-name>/.$desc: Isolated module — imports only from core or itself

mod-root.desc: public API, only external import surface

<module-name>.desc: module-level rune spec — the source this module is generated from

sig.desc: spec-owned signatures, regenerated by rune sync

test.desc: unit tests for the sibling mod

poly-mod.desc: barrel re-export for the active variant

mod.desc: exposes functionality to the outside world

e2e.test.desc: cypress end-to-end tests for this entry point

<name>.desc: class validator and class transformer type definition

spec/.$desc: rune staging area — authored specs (runes/), data design + cake artifacts (misc/), UI prototype (ui/), founding product docs (product/), the ratified contract's machine faces (contract/)

<name>.desc: rune spec for a module (legacy flat layout — prefer spec/runes/)

runes/.$desc: Rune spec files — one per module (the canonical authoring home; core.rune holds shared [SRV]s)

misc/.$desc: data design (data.json, data.review.html) + keep cake artifacts (cake.json, heal-rules.json, scenarios/)

ui/.$desc: sprig UI prototype + design system (sprig:prototype / sprig:design output)

product/.$desc: founding product docs — spec.md + user-stories.md (rune:scope output)

contract/.$desc: the ratified cross-repo contract's machine faces — generated OpenAPI + typed client, the prototype-seeded draft, the breakdown binding (queries + commands; see sprig's contract.md)

specs/.$desc: Rune spec files — one per module

fixtures/.$desc: Legacy cake-artifact home (used when the project has no spec/ dir): cake.json, heal-rules.json

heal-rules.desc: keep cake self-heal rules — rune-generated starter, merge-owned

app/.$desc: sprig UI app (frontend) — its own layout (src/pages, shell, islands) is owned and validated by sprig, not rune; rune hosts it via serve.ts (Bedrock). Ignored here like spec/ui

indent.summary: The columns `rune fmt` writes. Indentation is presentation: a line's kind is its first token, and only nesting is relative — a body line ([ENT] body [REQ], [PLY] cases) is indented deeper than its opener.

transports.summary: a co-located process (datastore, queue, object store)
an in-process runtime/std-lib boundary (filesystem, subprocess, crypto, clock) — neither a network surface nor a co-located process; its faults are synchronous throws and its env-var list is optional

faults.summary: A fault line is `! ` followed by space-separated fault names, directly under the step that raises it. A well-known name carries its HTTP status from this table; any other name must carry its own (`! card-expired=402`). Codegen emits one typed fault class per name; the runtime maps a thrown fault to its status. Each fault implies a test case; a step with no faults cannot fail.

wellKnown.summary: the write collides with current state
the service did not answer in time
the caller may not do this
the service could not be reached
any `invalid-<what>` (and `invalid` itself): the input is unprocessable
